analysis: The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md: it bumps the 'Last updated' date and adds a documentation section, 'GPT-OSS decode command buffers' (head lines ~4816-4826). The section describes GPT-OSS plain decode steps committing a Metal command buffer every 100 operations through GPTOSSDecodeCommandBuffers and CBv2DecodeCommandBufferLimitsProviding. It states that results do not depend on the partitioning and that prefill keeps MLX defaults. I reviewed the supplied excerpts, base lines 5337-5441 and head lines 1-419. The added section itself was not in the supplied head excerpt, but its text is visible in the patch. The changed text has no trust-boundary, key, attestation, encryption, authorization or data-exposure effects. It is documentation of a performance and scheduling tuning, and no code was supplied. The mention of the 10-in-flight command-buffer limit relates loosely to the availability concerns in T-029 and T-010. Nothing in the provided text weakens a mitigation or contradicts an existing threat-model assumption. Remaining unverified contract: the actual source change implementing the 100-op commit limit is not in this batch, so whether the claimed result-invariance holds, and whether a higher op count could affect decode latency or cancellation or fence-timing behavior, is not assessed. Other units may cover it. The cluster, Qwen TP and Nemotron prose in the excerpts is unchanged context. The existing T-041 and prefix-cache statements are unaffected.
